biography.plain_text: Calisto Tanzi was an Italian businessman who expanded his inherited family food business into Parmalat, the international dairy group based near Parma. He took over his father's ham business in 1961, when he was just twenty-two. Parmalat collapsed in 2003, and Tanzi was subsequently convicted of fraudulent bankruptcy and market-rigging.

long_biography.plain_text:
Milk that could be stored without refrigeration helped Calisto Tanzi take Parmalat beyond its local market. The company began producing long-life milk in 1966, using heat treatment that extended its shelf life to six months. Overseas expansion followed, including a sales drive in Brazil, while cheese and desserts broadened the product range.

Sport became a prominent part of Tanzi's marketing strategy. Parmalat sponsored skiing before linking its name to Niki Lauda and becoming Brabham's title sponsor in 1978. Tanzi also acquired Parma's football club, investing in players as it rose from Italy's second division to European competition; his son Stefano later became its president.

The specialist account calls it his father's ham business; Reuters compresses the earlier company into a family milk operation.
